references.text: The parallel text describing the instructions for the second row on the breastplate with the same precious stones: nofek, sapphire, and jashfeh (diamond).
Ezekiel's description of the king of Tyre's splendor mentions several of the same precious stones, including sapphire, which was on the priest's breastplate.
Sapphire is mentioned as a costly stone from the earth, showing the value of the stones on the breastplate.
Sapphire is described as more valuable than gold, emphasizing the importance of the precious stones on the high priest's breastplate.
The foundations of the new Jerusalem are adorned with precious stones, including sapphire as the second foundation stone, mirroring the second row of the breastplate.
